title: Negative prompts and cfg 1.0
hook: A negative prompt is not a subtraction of concepts. It replaces the unconditional branch, and with an ordinary sampler at cfg 1 it does nothing at all.

verified.claim: The negative fills the uncond slot of the cfg sum.
At cfg close to 1 the negative is not evaluated, unless a node or sampler sets disable_cfg1_optimization.
CFG++ samplers and SAG set that flag and then use the unconditional prediction.
ConditioningZeroOut sets the tensor and the pooled vector to zeros.
The three-class table is exact to every digit at cfg 1, as the lab asserts.

unchecked: We did not render the same seed with and without a negative. All our Sampling Lab renders use one negative, so no picture here shows what a negative prompt adds.
We did not measure how a zeroed negative and an encoded empty negative differ in a picture. We only read that their numbers differ.
